lines.text: Someone was running across the rooftops last night. Too light for a shinobi on patrol, my husband says.
The night watch found scratches on a door in the apartment block. Kids, they think. I'm not so sure.
There's a stone door at the foot of the Rock nobody's opened in my lifetime. My grandmother said not to ask.
The desk is passing round a name to watch for on the roads: Yūgure. Two-man teams, ash-violet cloaks. Keep your eyes open.
A merchant's cart came back from the east with a false floor. Paper in it, the gate guard said. Chakra paper.
The stadium's still closed. I can't walk past it without smelling the smoke.
They say the Hokage stood between the stands and the fire. Whatever happened after, the village owes that.
A new face will go up on the Rock. The masons are already measuring. It feels too soon.
